panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E photomicrograph of excised torus mandibularis (TM) tissue from a human patient, showing dense mature lamellar bone with lacunae and osteocytes, matching the torus mandibularis dense lamellar bone histology finding. Caption and in-text explicitly attribute the specimen to TM in an article focused on torus removal.
panels.attribution_text: Rocca et al. Er:YAG Laser: A New Technical Approach to Remove Torus Palatinus and Torus Mandibularis.. Case reports in dentistry 2012. doi:10.1155/2012/487802. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Photomicrograph of histological appearance of TM shows dense bony tissue, presence of lacunae and normal osteocytes (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification 200x).
in_text_mentions: Hard tissue fragment was submitted in 10% formalin for histopathologic examination. The examination of hematoxylin and eosin staining specimen revealed (Figure 4) dense, mature bony tissue, organized in wide lamellar pattern with scattered osteocytes and small marrow spaces.

findings.label: Bony exostosis on lingual aspect of mandible
findings.evidence: Visible bilateral bony exostoses on the lingual aspect of the mandible; caption states 'torus mandibularis bilateral combined'.

panels.rationale: Single clinical intraoral photograph showing classic bilateral mandibular tori on the lingual aspect of the mandible, with intact overlying mucosa and caption confirmation. [raw subtype: bilateral combined]
panels.attribution_text: Disha et al. Oral Tori Findings in an Adult Albanian Population: A Single-Center Pilot Study.. Dentistry journal 2024. doi:10.3390/dj12080242. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: A clinical photo showing torus mandibularis bilateral combined in a male subject.
in_text_mentions: Out of 48 patients with torus mandibularis (39.3%), 29 were female (37.7%) and 19 were male (42.2%). The most common pattern was solitary bilateral (47.9%), while the multiple unilateral form was the rarest (2.1%). Figure 2 shows torus mandibular bilateral solitary in a female subject and Figure 3 shows torus mandibularis bilateral combined. There was no significant difference in the pattern of torus mandibularis based on gender (p = 0.359).

in_text_mentions: A 59-years-old male was referred to the clinic (Laser Unit, Pôle Odontologique, Centre Hospitalier Universitaire St Roch, Nice, France) for evaluation and treatment.
